question: Francesca Albanese is the current Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian Territory occupied since 19671 at the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). The OHCHR website reads, ‘Throughout her mandate ... Albanese strives for impartiality and inclusiveness ... true impartiality cannot be either ignorance or indifference ...

it involves objectively investigating facts through the lens of international law and recognizing and addressing ... underlying power imbalance or historical injustices. Her focus is on achieving rights and freedoms, including through justice and accountability, for all involved.’2 Recently, Ms Albanese has been behaving in a non-inclusive manner.

For example, she walked out of a debate when reference was made to a Holocaust survivor, and she criticised a mayor who referred to the Israeli hostages. In the light of the above and the fact that the Commission contributes financially to the OHCHR: 1.
Does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy consider that Ms Albanese’s statements reflect the position of the European Union?

Could the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy approach the OHCHR to challenge the lack of impartiality and inclusiveness in Ms Albanese’s approach, which her recent behaviour has made evident?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.2.2026) The EU is a firm supporter of the multilateral rules-based international order with the UN at its core, including the UN human rights system and the independence of the UN Human Rights Council (UN HRC) special procedures’ mandate holders.

The EU cooperates with HRC mechanisms and fully respects their mandates and urges all states to do so, including the mandate of UN Special Rapporteurs (UNSR) on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian Territory occupied since 1967. UNSRs have an essential role in the fight against impunity and in ensuring accountability for serious human rights violations.

All UN special procedures mandate-holders must abide by the Code of conduct adopted by the UNHRC. The EU has repeatedly called for an end to attacks and threats against mandate-holders appointed by the Council.

The EU will continue to support efforts towards independent investigations into violations and abuses of human rights and violations of international humanitarian law, including those that may amount to international crimes.

With regard to the situation of human rights in the occupied Palestinian territory, the EU position has been reiterated on several occasion at different levels and through various statements, including during the 60th session of the Human Rights Council1.
